title: E-commerce: DesiCart Marketplace
description: DesiCart is a fictional Indian online marketplace selling electronics, fashion, home goods, beauty, grocery and books across 20 cities. The data covers two years of customers, orders, line items, payments and returns (Jan 2023 to Dec 2024), including festive-season sale spikes around Diwali and the usual messiness of a real order database. Use it for revenue analysis, cohort and repeat-purchase analysis, return analysis and cleaning practice.

tables.name: customers
tables.description: One row per registered customer (a few duplicated rows are deliberate).

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Customer identifier (primary key, chronological by signup)

columns.name: city
columns.description: Home city (inconsistent casing/whitespace, NULL for some)

columns.name: state
columns.description: Indian state of the city (NULL when city is NULL)

columns.name: signup_date_raw
columns.description: Signup date as typed in a legacy form: mixed formats, some NULL (for cleaning lessons)

columns.name: acquisition_channel
columns.description: Marketing channel that brought the customer

columns.name: is_prime
columns.description: 1 if customer holds the paid DesiCart Prime membership

tables.name: products
tables.description: Product catalogue (~420 SKUs).

columns.name: category
columns.description: Top-level category (a few rows have inconsistent casing/whitespace)

tables.name: orders
tables.description: One row per order (about 1% exact duplicate rows are deliberate).

columns.name: order_date
columns.description: Date the order was placed (clean ISO in SQLite)

columns.name: order_time
columns.description: Time of day the order was placed (HH:MM:SS)

columns.name: order_status
columns.description: Delivered, Cancelled or RTO (return to origin, mostly COD)

columns.name: sales_channel
columns.description: Android App, iOS App, Website or Mobile Web

columns.name: total_amount
columns.description: Order value in INR after discount and shipping

tables.name: order_items
tables.description: Line items of each order.

columns.name: unit_price
columns.description: Selling price per unit in INR after discount (a few 100x outliers)

tables.name: payments
tables.description: Payment attempts (some orders have a failed attempt followed by a success).

columns.name: payment_method
columns.description: UPI, Credit Card, Debit Card, COD, Netbanking or Wallet

columns.name: payment_date
columns.description: Date of payment (delivery date for COD)

tables.name: returns
tables.description: Returned line items.

qualityIssues: orders: ~1% of rows (about 100) are exact duplicates (same order_id repeated); so orders.order_id has no PRIMARY KEY constraint.
customers: 20 exact duplicate customer rows; customers.customer_id is therefore not unique.
customers.email is NULL for ~8% of rows, phone ~3%, gender ~4%, city ~3% (state is NULL whenever city is NULL).
customers.city: ~10% of values have inconsistent casing or stray whitespace ('mumbai', ' Mumbai', 'DELHI ').
customers.signup_date_raw: free-text dates in four formats (YYYY-MM-DD, DD/MM/YYYY, '5 Mar 2023', 'Mar 5, 2023') and ~3% NULL; signup_date holds the clean value.
products.category: ~2% of values have inconsistent casing or whitespace.
order_items.unit_price: 12 rows are 100x too high (entry errors) which inflates order totals for those orders.
CSV only - orders.order_date: ~18% of rows are written as DD-MM-YYYY instead of YYYY-MM-DD.
CSV only - orders.total_amount: ~12% of rows are text like '₹1,234.50' (symbol and thousands commas).
CSV only - returns.refund_amount: ~50% of rows are text with rupee symbol and Indian digit grouping (e.g. '₹1,23,456.00').
payments: ~5% of online-paid orders have an extra earlier 'Failed' attempt row, so order_id is not unique in payments.

signals: [Instructor note] Festive spikes: order volume rises ~1.5-1.9x in the Diwali windows (Oct 8-16 2023, Nov 6-14 2023, Sep 27-Oct 6 2024, Oct 24-Nov 3 2024); weekends are ~18% higher; steady growth through 2024.
[Instructor note] Fashion and Footwear have return rates of ~21% and ~15% (mostly 'Size / fit issue'), versus ~1% for Grocery.
[Instructor note] COD orders are cancelled ~11% of the time and RTO another ~7%, versus ~3.5% cancellation for prepaid.
[Instructor note] Tier-2 cities use COD far more (~34% vs ~18%) and have longer delivery times.
[Instructor note] Prime members (22% of customers) place roughly twice the orders; customer activity is heavy-tailed (a minority of customers drive most orders).
[Instructor note] Data-entry outliers (12 order_items with 100x unit_price) distort average order value unless handled.

title: Food Delivery: ThaliDash
description: ThaliDash is a fictional Indian food-delivery platform operating in 10 cities with 600 partner restaurants and 900 delivery partners. Two years of deliveries, ratings and promo redemptions capture lunch and dinner peaks, IPL-season surges and monsoon disruption. Use it to study delivery time, SLA breaches, customer ratings, partner performance and promo ROI.

tables.name: restaurants
tables.description: Partner restaurants.

columns.name: onboarded_date
columns.description: Date the restaurant joined the platform

tables.name: delivery_partners
tables.description: Delivery riders (a few duplicate rows are deliberate).

tables.name: deliveries
tables.description: One row per order/delivery (~0.8% exact duplicate rows are deliberate).

columns.name: actual_minutes
columns.description: Actual minutes from order to delivery (NULL if cancelled)

columns.name: delay_minutes
columns.description: actual_minutes minus promised_minutes (NULL if cancelled; negative = early)

columns.name: order_value
columns.description: Food order value in INR (8 rows are 100x outliers)

columns.name: payment_mode
columns.description: UPI, Card, Cash on Delivery or Wallet

columns.name: weather
columns.description: Clear, Cloudy, Rain or Heavy Rain at delivery

tables.name: ratings
tables.description: Customer ratings for ~60-70% of delivered orders.

tables.name: promo_usage
tables.description: Promo code redemptions on deliveries.

columns.name: is_new_user
columns.description: 1 if redemption by a first-time user

qualityIssues: deliveries: ~0.8% of rows (about 120) are exact duplicates by delivery_id, so delivery_id has no PRIMARY KEY constraint.
delivery_partners: 8 exact duplicate partner rows.
deliveries.actual_minutes, delay_minutes, delivered_time and cancel_reason are NULL by design for cancelled orders (~5-6% of rows).
deliveries.order_value: 8 rows are 100x outliers (e.g. 41,200 instead of 412).
restaurants.city ~8% and delivery_partners.city ~6% (and deliveries.city ~3%) have inconsistent casing or whitespace; restaurants.city ~2% NULL; delivery_partners.phone ~5% NULL.
promo_usage.promo_code: ~4% of values have inconsistent casing/whitespace.
CSV only - deliveries.order_time: ~15% of rows are DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM:SS instead of ISO.
CSV only - deliveries.order_value: ~15% of rows are text with rupee symbol and Indian grouping (e.g. '₹1,250').
CSV only - ratings.rated_at: ~25% of rows in DD-MM-YYYY format.
CSV only - promo_usage.discount_amount: ~20% of rows are text like '₹75.00'.

  }
  delivery_partners {
    INTEGER partner_id PK

  }

signals: [Instructor note] Delivery delay drives ratings: delivery_rating falls ~0.075 per minute of delay; late (delay > 10 min) orders average roughly 1-1.5 points lower than on-time orders; unhappy customers are also more likely to rate.
[Instructor note] Heavy Rain and Rain days (Mumbai/Kolkata/Pune Jun-Sep, Chennai Oct-Dec) add 6-13 minutes and raise cancellation rates (~3.5% base up to ~8%).
[Instructor note] Lunch (12-13h) and dinner (20-21h) peaks have longer waits; weekends are ~25% busier; order volume rises ~1.3x during IPL months (Mar 22-May 26 2024, Mar 31-May 28 2023).
[Instructor note] Partners in their first ~60 days are ~5 minutes slower; a skill factor per partner creates a spread in partner performance.

[Instructor note] FLAT75 is applied heavily to low-value orders (discount is a large share of order value), making it the worst-ROI promo; WELCOME50 drives new-user orders; IPLFEAST and MONSOON20 only appear in their seasons.
[Instructor note] Restaurant food quality varies independently of delivery speed (food_rating vs delivery_rating can be separated by analysts).
[Instructor note] 8 outlier order_values (100x) distort average order value.

title: HR Analytics: Nirmaan Technologies
description: Nirmaan Technologies is a fictional 2,400-person Indian tech and services company with eight departments across Bengaluru, Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai and Delhi. The dataset links employees to appraisal-cycle salary changes, half-yearly performance reviews and exits during 2023-2024. Use it to analyse attrition drivers, pay equity, hike policy and workforce planning.

tables.name: departments
tables.description: Eight departments with budget and head.

tables.name: employees
tables.description: One row per employee ever employed 2023-2024 (12 duplicate rows are deliberate).

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Employee identifier (duplicated for the duplicate rows)

columns.name: job_level
columns.description: Junior, Mid, Senior, Lead or Manager

columns.name: manager_id
columns.description: FK to employees.employee_id (NULL for top managers)

columns.name: employment_status
columns.description: Active or Exited (matches the attrition table)

tables.name: salaries
tables.description: Salary history: opening/joining CTC and April appraisal revisions.

columns.name: annual_ctc
columns.description: Annual cost-to-company in INR (5 rows are 100x outliers)

columns.name: hike_pct
columns.description: Percentage hike versus the previous CTC (NULL for opening/joining rows)

columns.name: change_reason
columns.description: Opening balance, Joining, Annual Appraisal or Promotion

tables.name: attrition
tables.description: One row per employee who left in 2023-2024.

columns.name: exit_type
columns.description: Resignation, Termination, Retirement or End of Contract

tables.name: performance_reviews
tables.description: Half-yearly reviews 2023-H1 to 2024-H1 (10 duplicate rows are deliberate).

columns.name: avg_monthly_overtime_hours
columns.description: Average monthly overtime hours in the period

qualityIssues: employees: 12 exact duplicate rows (same employee_id twice), so employee_id has no PRIMARY KEY constraint; performance_reviews: 10 exact duplicate rows.
employees.gender: ~6% of rows use 'M'/'F' instead of 'Male'/'Female'.
employees.city: ~9% have inconsistent casing/whitespace ('pune', ' Pune'), ~2% NULL; employees.email ~4% NULL.
employees.manager_id is NULL for top-level managers (~5% of employees).
salaries.annual_ctc: 5 rows are 100x outliers (e.g. 120,000,000 instead of 1,200,000).
salaries.hike_pct is NULL for opening-balance and joining rows (about 45% of salary rows).
attrition.exit_interview_score is NULL for ~30% of exits.
CSV only - employees.hire_date and employees.date_of_birth: ~20% of rows are DD-MM-YYYY.
CSV only - salaries.annual_ctc: ~30% of rows are text with rupee symbol and Indian grouping (e.g. '₹12,50,000').
CSV only - performance_reviews.review_date: ~15% of rows are DD-MM-YYYY.

signals: [Instructor note] Attrition is driven by (a) low manager ratings, (b) high average overtime (> ~10 h/month), and (c) low appraisal hikes (< ~4%); employees with all three leave at several times the base rate.
[Instructor note] Customer Support, Sales and Operations have the highest attrition; Finance and HR the lowest; employees with < 2 years tenure leave more.
[Instructor note] Exits spike in April-June (post-appraisal) and Nov-Jan (post-bonus).
[Instructor note] Hike % tracks performance (about +3 points per rating step) while Sales gets ~1 point lower hikes.
[Instructor note] Customer Support has the lowest CTC but the highest overtime; Engineering and Product pay ~25-30% more than average.
[Instructor note] Overtime-heavy exits cite 'Work-life balance / overtime' far more often in exit_reason.
[Instructor note] 5 salary outliers (100x) distort average CTC unless excluded.

title: Fintech: UPI-style Payments (PayZippy and friends)
description: A fictional UPI-style digital payments ecosystem with five payment apps, eight banks and 400 merchants across India. Transactions cover P2P transfers, merchant payments, bill payments and recharges over two years, with salary-day, festive and evening peaks plus four NammaPay outages. Use it for failure-rate analysis, peak-hour load, merchant category insights and simple fraud-flag exploration.

tables.description: App users (10 duplicate rows are deliberate).

columns.name: kyc_status
columns.description: Full KYC, Min KYC or Pending

columns.name: preferred_app
columns.description: UPI app the user mostly uses

tables.name: merchants
tables.description: Merchants accepting UPI.

tables.name: transactions

columns.name: receiver_user_id

columns.name: txn_type
columns.description: P2M, P2P, Bill Pay or Recharge

columns.name: amount

transactions.amount: 6 rows are 100x outliers.
transactions.merchant_id is NULL for P2P rows (~24%) and receiver_user_id is NULL for non-P2P rows - by design, not an error.
users.city ~10% inconsistent casing/whitespace and ~3% NULL; users.phone ~2% NULL; users.upi_id ~5% NULL; merchants.city ~8% inconsistent casing.
failed_transactions.retry_succeeded is NULL when retried = 0 (~40% of rows).
CSV only - users.signup_date: ~15% of rows are DD-MM-YYYY.
CSV only - transactions.txn_datetime: ~15% DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM:SS; transactions.amount: ~12% text with rupee symbol and Indian grouping.
CSV only - failed_transactions.failed_at: ~20% DD-MM-YYYY.

signals: [Instructor note] Kaveri Co-op Bank has a much higher failure rate than other banks, concentrated in peak hours (9-10h and 18-20h) with code BANK_SERVER_TIMEOUT (about 15% at peak vs ~2% elsewhere).

[Instructor note] NammaPay had four outage windows (2023-03-14 10-13h, 2023-09-21 18-22h, 2024-02-06 9-12h, 2024-07-16 19-22h). Inside them about 42% of NammaPay attempts fail with UPI_SYSTEM_DOWN, vs ~2-3% normally.
[Instructor note] Failures are ~35% higher on the 1st-3rd of the month (salary days) and amounts above 50,000 fail 2.5x more (LIMIT_EXCEEDED).
[Instructor note] Volume spikes around Diwali windows and month-end; weekends are ~10% higher; evening 18-20h is the busiest slot.
[Instructor note] Network/timeouts are retried and succeed far more often than insufficient-funds failures.

[Instructor note] About 1.5% of transactions are flagged (is_flagged = 1). Flags cluster in late-night hours (23h-4h), in accounts less than 30 days old, when an amount is more than 3x the payer's usual median, and for Electronics, Travel and Entertainment merchants. Large late-night P2P transfers (> 8,000) are the strongest signal (~30% flagged).
[Instructor note] Customer activity is heavy-tailed; merchant volume is power-law distributed; Fuel/Travel/Electronics have high ticket sizes.

title: Subscription App: Kahani+ Streaming
description: Kahani+ is a fictional Indian streaming and learning app with a 7-day free trial and Basic, Standard and Premium plans (monthly or annual, priced in INR). The data tracks 5,200 signups from 2023-2024 through trial, first payment, renewals and cancellation, along with a raw event log. Use it for funnel conversion, retention curves, cohort analysis, churn drivers and plan mix.

tables.description: One row per signup (8 duplicate rows are deliberate).

columns.name: platform
columns.description: Android, iOS or Web at signup

tables.description: One row per user who started a free trial; tracks conversion, renewal and end.

columns.name: paid_start_date

columns.name: end_date

columns.name: cancel_date

columns.name: renewal_count
columns.description: Number of successful renewals after the first payment

tables.name: events
tables.description: Raw product and billing event log (~0.5% exact duplicates).

columns.name: event_name
columns.description: signup, trial_start, trial_expired, payment_success, renewal_success, payment_failed, cancel_subscription, app_open, content_view, search (some UPPERCASE)

columns.name: platform

events.event_name: ~1.2% of values are UPPERCASE ('APP_OPEN'); events.platform: ~2% are lowercase ('android') - breaks naive GROUP BY.
users.email ~6% NULL; users.city ~4% NULL and ~10% inconsistent casing/whitespace.

events.plan is NULL for events before a plan is chosen (signup and most early engagement events); subscriptions.paid_start_date NULL for users who never paid; cancel_date/end_date NULL by design for active users.

signals: [Instructor note] Funnel: signup -> trial_start (~63%) -> payment_success (~36% of trials) -> renewals; iOS converts trials noticeably better (~50%) than Android (~34%).
[Instructor note] The March 2024 signup cohort churns far faster (about 2.7x hazard) - month-1 and month-2 retention is visibly worse than neighbouring cohorts.
[Instructor note] Influencer-sourced users start trials often but convert at less than half the normal rate and churn faster; Referral users convert ~25% better.
[Instructor note] Basic plan churns more than Premium; annual plans have almost no churn in the first year but low renewal at month 12.
[Instructor note] Oct-Nov (Diwali) cohorts convert ~20% better; signups grow strongly through 2024.
[Instructor note] About 3.5% of renewal charges fail (payment_failed), and ~45% of those lead to involuntary cancellation.
[Instructor note] Engagement events (app_open, content_view) cluster in the first 14 days after signup and decay for churners.

The data links campaign budgets and daily spend to clicks and conversions, plus a separate 12,000-user checkout A/B test (free-shipping banner). Use it for ROAS and CAC analysis, channel comparison, attribution-style funnels and A/B test significance testing.

signals: [Instructor note] Campaign 'Influencer Mega Reach Oct-24' burns the largest budget at ~2.3x normal CPC with a conversion rate ~1/8 of a normal influencer campaign - by far the worst ROAS/CAC among revenue-driving campaigns (ROAS about 0.07 vs 5-8 for Search).
[Instructor note] Email and WhatsApp have the lowest CPC and the highest conversion rate (best ROAS); Google Search is the best large-scale paid channel.
[Instructor note] Diwali windows (Oct 25-Nov 14 2023, Oct 20-Nov 3 2024) lift conversion rate by ~25%; Search/Meta Diwali campaigns are the top revenue campaigns.
[Instructor note] Awareness-objective campaigns (YouTube, Display) convert to Signup/Lead mostly and look weak on last-click revenue.
[Instructor note] Desktop converts ~35% better than mobile; Metro converts better than Tier-2.

[Instructor note] A/B test: treatment lifts conversion from ~9.5% to ~11% overall (about +1.5pp, p roughly 0.01-0.03), driven by Mobile (about +1.8pp) while Desktop shows an insignificant +0.3pp; treatment AOV is ~4% lower (free shipping cost), so revenue per user lift is smaller than conversion lift.
[Instructor note] Contaminated users, duplicates and 100x spend outliers must be cleaned before computing cost metrics or test statistics.

title: Retail Sales: Vasudha Retail
description: Vasudha Retail is a fictional chain of 24 grocery and lifestyle stores (hypermarkets, supermarkets and express stores) across 15 Indian states and union territories. The dataset covers 2023-2024 with sampled transaction lines, month-end inventory snapshots per store and SKU, and monthly sales targets. Use it for monthly sales trends, festive seasonality, stockout impact, overstock and target attainment.

tables.name: stores
tables.description: 24 stores with city, region, format and carpet area.

columns.name: store_code
columns.description: Short store code such as VSD-001

tables.name: sales
tables.description: Sampled sales transaction lines, about one line per store per day (350 exact duplicate rows are deliberate).

columns.name: sale_id
columns.description: Sale line identifier (duplicated for duplicate rows)

columns.name: sale_datetime
columns.description: Date and time of the sale

columns.name: sku_id
columns.description: SKU code (no product master table; see category)

columns.name: net_amount_inr
columns.description: Net line amount in INR after discount (6 rows are 100x outliers)

columns.name: payment_mode
columns.description: UPI, Card, Cash or Wallet (casing issues, ~1% NULL)

tables.name: inventory
tables.description: Month-end stock snapshot for every store and SKU, 2023-01 to 2024-12.

columns.name: stock_on_hand
columns.description: Units on hand at month end (NULL for ~1%)

columns.name: days_out_of_stock
columns.description: Days during the month the SKU was out of stock

tables.name: targets
tables.description: Monthly net sales targets per store; the East region (Kolkata, Patna, Guwahati) has no targets.

columns.name: target_net_sales_inr
columns.description: Target net sales in INR (NULL for ~3%)

columns.name: target_units
columns.description: Target units derived from the sales target

qualityIssues: sales: 350 exact duplicate rows (same sale_id twice), so sale_id has no PRIMARY KEY constraint.
sales.discount_pct: NULL for ~4% of rows; net_amount_inr already reflects the discount, so it is still populated.
sales.payment_mode: ~8% inconsistent casing/whitespace ('upi', ' Card'), ~1% NULL.
sales.net_amount_inr: 6 rows are 100x outliers.
stores.city: ~8% casing/whitespace issues.
inventory.stock_on_hand: ~1% NULL.
targets.target_net_sales_inr: ~3% NULL; no targets exist for the East region stores.
CSV only - sales.sale_datetime: ~15% of rows use DD-MM-YYYY; sales.net_amount_inr: ~25% are rupee text with Indian grouping.
CSV only - inventory.snapshot_date: ~12% of rows use DD-MM-YYYY; targets.target_net_sales_inr: ~15% are rupee text.
No product master table: sku_id and category are denormalised codes.

signals: [Instructor note] Stockouts: Velachery (Chennai), Adajan (Surat), Gomti Nagar (Lucknow) and Kharadi (Pune) stores have frequent stockouts (days_out_of_stock > 0 for many SKUs) and roughly 30% lower sales volume than peers.
[Instructor note] Diwali (Oct-Nov) and the 2024 Navratri window spike sales; Republic Day and Independence Day sale weeks give smaller spikes.
[Instructor note] Home Decor is slow-moving: about 5% of sales volume, but stock covers 6-10 months of demand, so it is overstocked.
[Instructor note] East region stores (Kolkata, Patna, Guwahati) have no targets, so target attainment can only be compared for the other regions.
[Instructor note] Targets are set at 90-115% of actual sales, so attainment clusters near 100% with a few misses.
[Instructor note] 2024 prices are about 6% higher than 2023 for every SKU, so compare volume and value separately.
[Instructor note] Sales are a sampled extract of about one transaction line per store per day, so use rates and shares rather than absolute totals.
[Instructor note] 6 net_amount outliers (100x) distort totals unless excluded.
